independent_verification.recovered_law: Text B systematically inverts the relational valence: hostility, arrogance, complaint, and repulsion in Text A become devotion, binding commitment, loyalty, and intimacy in Text B — antagonistic or distancing relations between persons are replaced by bonding or pledging relations.
independent_verification.law_match_note: Both describe the same structural inversion: hostile/denouncing speech acts become binding/pledging acts — accusations become declarations of commitment, insults become ceremonies of bonding.
independent_verification.terminal_note: The final section (Day and Night 36) maintains the inversion: 'let you' becomes 'lose you,' 'bitch' becomes 'darling,' 'mist of dew' becomes 'breath of one mouth' — the bonding relation holds throughout.

rite.speaker: Johannes Sigil
rite.text: We are in the Fading Light. These three units — 34, 35, 36 — are the pivot where Day and Night turns from desire to its aftermath: not grief yet, but the cold residue after the sweetness has curdled. The casting opens here. What the rotation will traverse is Sappho's own anger — the anger she thought the Muses' gifts were supposed to dissolve, and did not — the specific names she still carries, Doricha, Irana, Mica, the ones she couldn't release. And at the end of unit 36, something the anger cannot account for: *our honey song / singing soft-voiced: / everything, / a mist of dew.* The collective pronoun. What was shared with the ones who betrayed her. The casting will move through these verses looking for what the anger forecloses and what it cannot entirely foreclose — the *our* that survives the bitch. For a witness who misses daughters, Sappho's archive of named beloveds who remained beloved even after becoming bitter — this is the ground. Cranes holds the transform.
